text:
**Data-quality findings, exclusions and assumptions**

- **Rows:** 60 total. Exclusions removed 15 trial rows (`is_trial = yes`) and 5 internal test rows (`@ourco.test`), leaving 40 paid rows (20 Basic, 20 Pro). The 5 test accounts were all Pro at 69 and all cancelled in Aug 2026, so leaving them in would have inflated the jump.
- **Clean checks:** No duplicate account IDs or emails, no cancel_month before signup_month, and every Basic row is at 19 USD. Pro rows are only 49 or 69.
- **Price points don't line up with signup date:** 8 of the 16 Pro accounts that signed up before the July increase (Mar–Jun) show 69, even though the increase hadn't happened yet. All 8 cancelled in Aug or Sep. The other 8 pre-July Pro accounts are at 49, and 7 of them are still active. The one exception is 1018, which cancelled in May at 49, before the increase.
- **What that implies:** I can't tell whether 69 means "existing customers were moved to the new price" or "the price field was updated at cancellation". Either way, 49 versus 69 is confounded with who stayed and who left. 49 may be grandfathered customers, and 69 may be everyone else.
- **As-of date:** I assumed the data runs through 2026-09-30 because the latest cancel_month is 2026-09. If September is incomplete, September churn is understated.
- **Denominators:** Churn rate = cancels in the month ÷ paid accounts active at the start of that month. Mar has no denominator. Rates with denominators under 10 are flagged as not meaningful.

**Churn by month (paid accounts only)**

| Month | Pro cancels / active | Pro at 49 | Pro at 69 | Basic cancels / active |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Apr | 0/4 (n.m.) | – | – | 0/4 (n.m.) |
| May | 1/8 (n.m.) | 1/8 | – | 0/8 (n.m.) |
| Jun | 0/11 | 0/11 | – | 1/12 (8%) |
| Jul | 0/15 | 0/15 | – | 1/15 (7%) |
| Aug | 7/19 (37%) | 0/7 | 7/12 (58%) | 2/18 (11%) |
| Sep | 3/12 (25%) | 0/7 | 3/5 (60%, n.m.) | 0/16 |

Note: In May the single cancel was at 49. The 69 price only appears in Aug–Sep cancels, so the Apr–Jul 69 cells are empty.

**Summary**

- **Answer: the jump is real in this sample, but the data can't show it was caused by the price increase. Confidence: low.** There are only 10 Pro cancels in Aug–Sep (against 1 in Apr–Jul), and price is tangled up with who stayed and who left.
- **What the data shows:**
  - Pro churn went from about 3% a month in Apr–Jul (1 cancel across 38 account-months) to 32% in Aug–Sep (10 cancels across 31 account-months).
  - All 10 Aug–Sep Pro cancels were at 69, and none of the 14 account-months at 49 cancelled.
  - Basic churn did not rise: 5% in Apr–Jul (2 cancels across 39 account-months) against 6% in Aug–Sep (2 cancels across 34). That fits a Pro-specific cause, which is consistent with the price but doesn't prove it.
- **What it only suggests:** The timing, the Pro-only rise and the absence of cancels at 49 all point toward the price increase. But the 69 group looks like the people the increase hit, or possibly a field recorded at cancellation, so the 49 versus 69 comparison is not a fair test. Alternative explanations the data can't rule out include a Pro product or competitor change, a seasonal or tenure effect (every Aug–Sep Pro cancel signed up 2–6 months earlier), and trial-driven or promo-driven signup cohorts.
- **Sample size:** After exclusions there are 20 Pro accounts and 11 Pro cancels in total. Only 5 Pro accounts at 69 were active entering September, so the 60% September figure is not meaningful on its own. This is a small pasted sample and not a basis for a firm decision.
- **To firm this up:** Get the full dataset, plus the date each account's price changed (not just the current price). Then compare churn for existing customers who got the increase against new July signups, and against any customers who stayed at 49.

**Suggested chart**

A line chart with the month (Mar–Sep 2026) on the x-axis and monthly churn rate (%) on the y-axis. Draw three lines: Pro at 49, Pro at 69 and Basic, with a vertical marker at July 2026 for the price increase. Label each point with its counts (e.g. "7/12") and show months with fewer than 10 active accounts as hollow markers. The CEO should notice that the Pro 69 line jumps after the marker while Basic stays flat. They should also see that the Pro 49 line stays at zero and that the hollow markers mean the numbers are small.
